title: SOC 2 / ISO27001 posture review - Stellar Commerce control mapping & KMS flow
summary: Redwood walked through how artifacts and Trust Center access map to Stellar's SOC2/ISO requirements. Customer asked detailed questions about RBAC delegation, SSO service accounts, KMS envelope encryption flow, and retention of audit logs for their EU customers. We agreed next steps: share SOC2 Type II report, scoped control matrix, and a KMS flow diagram; schedule technical walkthrough with DevOps for key rotation/demo.
action_items: Lena Ortiz - Share SOC 2 Type II report and trust-center link - due 2027-01-18
Marcus Yi - Produce KMS envelope encryption diagram showing customer key flow and HSM/KMS integration - due 2027-01-21
Priya Kulkarni - Send RBAC/SSO quickstart doc with SAML examples and support contacts - due 2027-01-19
Jon Park (customer) - Provide list of compliance stakeholders and target audit window - due 2027-01-20
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack and SOC2 Type II PDF
Schedule DevOps deep dive (Marcus + Rina) week of Jan 25
Customer to confirm whether keys will be customer-managed or Redwood-managed
Agree on log retention window for EU data and send sample log export
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz; Marcus Yi; Priya Kulkarni; Derek Shaw; Amira Khan; Jon Park; Rina Lopez

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call and then we'll dive into posture and the trust center access questions. Marcus will cover the KMS flow, Priya will cover the access bits.
[00:18] Derek Shaw: Yep, thanks. We're mostly here to validate controls mapping to our ISO and SOC2 scope. We have an audit window in Q2 so want to make sure evidence paths are clear.
[00:32] Marcus Yi: Great. I'll start with a high level of how encryption works in Redwood when customer opts for CMK or Redwood-managed keys. Quick disclaimer, I'll try not to get too deep yet.
[00:46] Amira Khan: Sorry, CMK means customer-managed key, right? We want CMK for EU data.
[00:55] Marcus Yi: Correct, CMK. When CMK is chosen, the customer owns the KMS key in their cloud tenant or HSM; Redwood wraps model- artifacts with envelope encryption. There is a KMS API call to decrypt the data at inference time, and the KV cache does not persist plaintext.
[01:15] Rina Lopez: Wait, when you say KV cache, do you mean the inference cache? We need to be sure nothing ends up in a shared cache across tenants.
[01:26] Marcus Yi: Right, good call. Our production runs per-tenant KV stores; there is no cross-tenant leakage. To be explicit, we partition caches by customer ID and keyspace. Sometimes transcripts show it as V K cache, weirdly.
[01:40] Jon Park: How do you handle key rotation without downtime?
[01:45] Marcus Yi: We have a key-rotation flow where a new key can be staged and then a rewrap job migrates stored envelopes. For live sessions we support multi-key lookups for a transition window so no outage. We'll diagram that.
[02:00] Lena Ortiz: On Trust Center access, we can grant read-only artifact access to specific emails or a SAML group. Priya, can you jump in?
[02:08] Priya Kulkarni: Sure. Trust Center supports role-based access. We map SAML attributes to RBAC roles; common mapping: auditors -> read-only reports; engineers -> deployment logs; infra -> full trace with masking. You can do group-based grants from your IdP.
[02:28] Derek Shaw: Is it possible to scope Trust Center to only show EU artifacts for EU auditors? We need data residency segregation for compliance.
[02:36] Priya Kulkarni: Currently, Trust Center has region filters and we can create view-scoped roles. It's not perfect like a separate instance, but it filters artifact lists and you can restrict access by tag. For strict segregation, our Private/VPC option is recommended.
[02:56] Amira Khan: Ok, good to know. We'll discuss Private option with procurement.
[03:05] Jon Park: On audit logs — retention and export — what's supported?
[03:10] Marcus Yi: We retain audit logs for 90 days by default in hosted, with add-ons for extended retention. Logs include request metadata, model, route, tokens billed, and error traces. We also support direct log forwarding to your SIEM via SSE or syslog.
[03:32] Rina Lopez: Can logs be stored in our EU bucket for residency?
[03:36] Marcus Yi: Yes, for Dedicated or Private deployments we can ship logs to your storage. In hosted, we can push a continuous export to your endpoint. There are some s3 endpoint config steps.
[03:48] Derek Shaw: About the artifact list in the trust center — will we get a signed artifact manifest for SOC2 evidence?
[03:55] Priya Kulkarni: Yes, for audits we can generate signed manifests and provide time-stamped evidence packages. We also maintain a change history for controls.
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: Some customers ask for continuous access for auditors versus one-time bundles; we support both.
[04:12] Derek Shaw: Brilliant. One more: RBAC delegation. We want to delegate limited admin to our infra team but not to product. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[04:21] Priya Kulkarni: We have about a dozen built-in roles and custom role creation; permissions are at the route and model level, plus Trust Center artifact scopes. You can deny key management ops to product teams while allowing them to deploy models.
[04:36] Amira Khan: Does that include restricting function calls / tool calls? We are concerned about exfil via tool integrations.
[04:43] Marcus Yi: Tool calling is controlled by route policies; you can disable tool calls per route or require explicit allow lists. We can show examples in the RBAC quickstart doc.
[04:58] Jon Park: On SSO, we're using SAML 2.0 with Okta. Any gotchas?
[05:03] Priya Kulkarni: Okta is well supported. Map the groups, send us the metadata URL, we set up the IdP connection; note that attribute mapping is case-sensitive in older consoles. Some customers experienced mapping mismatches — transcript tends to show S S O as SSO as 'ess ess oh' sometimes.
[05:24] Rina Lopez: About encryption at rest for model weights and artifacts — are those encrypted with our key if we choose CMK?
[05:32] Marcus Yi: Yes, artifacts at rest are encrypted with the CMK; we re-encrypt during key rotation. For hosted we use envelope encryption; for Private deployments, keys can be fully customer-hosted.
[05:48] Derek Shaw: Can you confirm whether audit logs include full prompt text? We need to redact PII by default for EU customers.
[05:57] Marcus Yi: By default, logs capture request metadata and a hashed summary of prompt content. We can enable full prompt logging but that's opt-in; for GDPR-sensitive workloads we recommend token-level redaction and PII scrubbing pipelines.
[06:18] Lena Ortiz: OK, maybe we should pause and call out the main risks Derek flagged: key ownership, log residency, and auditor access. Anything else?
[06:28] Jon Park: Also the evidence bundle format — we need a manifest that ties controls to artifacts.
[06:33] Priya Kulkarni: We will produce a control mapping spreadsheet that maps your control IDs to Redwood artifacts and evidence types.
[06:44] Amira Khan: Timeline question: can you get that to us before Jan 25?
[06:48] Lena Ortiz: We'll aim for Jan 18 for the primary docs. Marcus will follow with the KMS diagram by Jan 21.
[07:00] [crosstalk] Marcus Yi: Also, if you want a short proof-of-concept with a scoped dataset we can run a mini-check to demonstrate encryption and log export.
[07:10] Derek Shaw: That could help for the auditors.
[07:15] Rina Lopez: On the DevOps deep dive, can we include a small runbook for key rotation and emergency key revocation?
[07:22] Marcus Yi: Absolutely, we'll draft a runbook and include command examples for your KMS provider.
[07:30] Lena Ortiz: Great. Any other questions?
[07:33] Jon Park: One last on SLA and incident logs — do you provide post-mortem artifacts?
[07:39] Priya Kulkarni: For Dedicated contracts we include incident post-mortems and timelines as part of the trust artifacts. Hosted customers can purchase extended incident reporting.
[07:50] Derek Shaw: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:54] Lena Ortiz: I'll recap next steps in an email and attach the SOC2 report. We'll follow up on scheduling the DevOps deep dive.
[08:02] Amira Khan: Thanks all.

Note: Transcript contains occasional mis-words and transcription artifacts; some technical terms were corrected in post call notes.
